title: spec(ui): `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES` has no row for `containsCaseInsensitive` → `icontains`, the one objectui filter-builder spelling the protocol's alias table lacks
body:
A bare card, filed by the objectui `domain:ui` execution seat (seat 1, session `session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`) as ruling `5748934939` on objectstack-ai/objectui#9559 orders. The ruling is maintainer-ratified in `5814267184`, 「同意」. ⛔ Not graded and not routed: `domain:*`, `priority:*` and `type` are the triage seat's.

## The ruling's words (verbatim)

「The three genuine protocol gaps stay as they are: `exists` / `notExists` remain opt-in with their named upstream blocker, and `containsCaseInsensitive` → `icontains` is an alias the protocol's table lacks — the claiming seat files that one spelling as a bare card in objectstack (spec alias table), ⛔ not fixed in objectui.」

## Fact (read on `main` at `d4c897e0`, and objectui `origin/main` at `e6203d756`)

- `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`: `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES` has no `containsCaseInsensitive` row. `normalizeFilterOperator('containsCaseInsensitive')` therefore returns the input verbatim, and `ViewFilterRuleSchema` refuses it.
- The objectui filter builder (`packages/components/src/custom/filter-builder.tsx`) has offered the id `containsCaseInsensitive` ("Contains (ignore case)") since objectui#4023, shipped in `@object-ui/components` 17.6.0 per its CHANGELOG. `FilterConditionField` lowers it to `$icontains`.
- objectstack-ai/objectui PR #10465 (in review) derives objectui's view-filter mirror from `ViewFilterRuleSchema`'s own operator member. After it lands, 19 of the builder's 22 ids validate and normalise; this spelling is one of the three that do not.

## ⚠️ The premise to check before adding the row

The table's own docblock sets the rule for a row: 「`icontains` (#8934) deliberately has NO rows here: this table bridges spellings that already live in stored metadata, and a canonical operator born after the table has none — inventing "synonyms" for it would widen the authoring surface rather than bridge a legacy one. … the folds exist per measured legacy spelling, not per operator.」

So whoever takes this card measures first: does `containsCaseInsensitive` live in stored VIEW metadata? The objectui builder lists it in `OPT_IN_OPERATORS`, offered only to `FilterConditionField` (the Mongo-criteria dialect), not to the list toolbar's view dialect. Stored view rules carrying it would come from before that restriction (objectui#4736) or from hand or AI authoring.
- **Measured present** ⇒ add the row, per the ruling.
- **Measured absent** ⇒ report that on this card and on objectstack-ai/objectui#9559, because the ruling's premise is then false. ⛔ Don't add a synonym the docblock refuses without that answer.

Re-check commands:
- `git grep -n containsCaseInsensitive -- packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` ⇒ 0 today.
- `git -C` an objectui checkout: `grep -n containsCaseInsensitive packages/components/src/custom/filter-builder.tsx` ⇒ the builder row and the `OPT_IN_OPERATORS` member.

## Dedupe

REST page walk over the 1000 most recently updated objectstack items (oldest `updated_at` 2026-09-20). `containsCaseInsensitive` ⇒ 0. `icontains` near `alias` ⇒ 0. `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES` ⇒ 0. Must-hit control `icontains` ⇒ 18 hits, none about the alias table.
